swag-golf.name: Swag Golf
src: On 25 August, Swag Golf published sixty-two licensed college pieces in a single day — fairway covers, driver covers, desk caddies and six miniature tour-bag coolers, spread across fifteen schools. It is the largest licensed run any brand in our universe has put out at once, and it landed the week college football started.

What makes it more than a logo exercise is the naming. Almost nothing here is called the Texas Cover or the Georgia Cover. They are called Hook 'Em, Between The Hedges, Hoo Hoo Hoosiers, Get Out Of Our Swamp, Walk Of Champions, OH-IO, Geaux Tigers. Swag licensed the marks and then went looking for what the student section actually shouts, which is a harder brief and a much better one.

The first is that Swag paints rather than prints. The mascots on the driver covers are rendered with visible brushwork — the Georgia bulldogs, the Miami ibis, the Ohio State buckeyes are each drawn rather than dropped in at scale. At arm's length on a bag that difference is the entire product.

The pricing, by the way, is a Swag habit rather than anything to do with the colleges: $99.99, $222.22, and $777.77 for the $10M Dollar Lance putter the brand put out two days after this program. The repeating digits are the house signature.
It is a Swag house convention rather than anything to do with the colleges. The covers are $99.99, the coolers $222.22, and the $10M Dollar Lance putter the brand released two days later was $777.77.
Yes — the products are listed by school name on Swag's own storefront, which is how licensed collegiate merchandise has to be sold.

takomo-golf.name: Takomo Golf
src: Takomo launched in 2021 out of Turku, Finland with a premise that shouldn't be radical but somehow still is: forged irons, clean design, half the price. No pro shop markup, no retail middlemen, no tour-van mythology. They design the clubs, partner with top-tier foundries, and ship direct. The savings go straight to the price tag — a full set of S20C forged cavity backs for $649, when comparable Japanese-forged sets from Mizuno or Srixon run well north of a thousand.

The lineup spans every skill level. The 101 MKII is a hollow-body game-improvement iron that won MyGolfSpy's Best GI Iron — serious forgiveness at $579 for a seven-piece set. The 201T MKII, new for 2026, is a players precision iron aimed at better ball strikers who want workability without giving up distance. And the 301 CB is the crown jewel: single-billet S20C carbon steel, forged and finished with the kind of feel you associate with boutique Japanese smithing, not a DTC brand that also sells $15 gloves. Wesley Bryan played Takomo irons on the PGA Tour. The Skyforger wedge, at $99, uses the same 8620 steel alloy that Cleveland and Vokey charge nearly double for.

The Scandinavian design DNA shows up everywhere — minimal branding, matte finishes, clean toplines. No loud graphics, no oversized cavities screaming for attention. Takomo makes the case that the traditional equipment pricing model is broken, and then they prove it by shipping clubs that perform alongside irons three times their price. If you haven't heard of them yet, you will.

Takomo spent its first years as an irons company. The 101, the 201 and the 301 covered game improvement through to blades, all forged, all sold direct out of Turku at prices that undercut the houses making comparable heads. That remains the centre of the business.
Takomo prints a target handicap range on every iron page, which makes the range unusually easy to read from the outside. The quoted lines below are the brand's own; the note under each is ours.

Sebastian Haapahovi founded the company in 2021 and it is based in Turku, Finland. YouTuber Grant Horvat has taken an ownership stake in the brand, and George and Wesley Bryan worked with Takomo on the Skyforger wedges.

twentyfour-golf.name: TwentyFour Golf
src: TwentyFour Golf is a Gold Coast label that sells golf caps, and then a few clothes. That is not a slight — it is the shape of the catalogue. Eighteen of its twenty-four products are hats, and the six garments sit on top of a cap line that is almost permanently sold out.

The collection's stated ambition is bigger than its footprint: TwentyFour Golf started with one idea: Australian golf deserved a brand that treated it seriously. Not stuffy. Not bargain-bin. A brand with a point of view. Fifteen pieces went out in the drop, eight of them caps across two silhouettes.

Why TwentyFour. The brand has never explained the name. An earlier version of this page offered a reading of it as though it were the brand's own; that was ours, not theirs, and it has been removed. The tagline is Always In Play and a homepage section reads THE GAME NEVER STOPS, which points somewhere, but pointing is not stating.

vessel.name: VESSEL
src: Jones leads with the 2026 Trouper 4.0 ($315) and the Heritage Trouper ($375) — two different takes on the same obsessive design philosophy. MacKenzie's 8-inch Waxed Canvas Mac ($740) is the heirloom play. Vessel's Lux Stand ($399), Stitch's SL2 Gen 2 ($398), and Shapland's Kantle 3.1 ($490) hold the premium middle. The lineup opens with Metalwood Studio 's adidas MC70 — a Predator upper on a golf chassis — and runs through Quiet Golf 's Samba, Eastside Golf's Jordan AJ1 Low, Malbon's in-house Tour 1, and three Nike retros that belong on a course as much as they do on concrete. PAYNTR shows up three times through collabs with Students Golf , Sugarloaf Social Club , and Vessel — each one engineered differently, each one carrying a different brand's DNA. Thirteen shoes, thirteen stories, $125 to $250.

The partners run from Students and Sugarloaf Social Club through Jones, Khalhon, Bad Birdie, Vessel, Ghost, Forresters, Matchstick and Del Campo, at prices from an eighteen dollar sock to a two hundred and fifty dollar shoe. Twenty-five that are still listed, across eleven partners: Sugarloaf Social Club, Jones Sports Co, Khalhon, Bad Birdie, Students Golf, Vessel, Ghost Golf, Forresters, Par x Design, Matchstick Golf and Del Campo.

Eighteen towels from fifteen brands, and every one of them would look better clipped to your bag than whatever came free with your last driver purchase. Sentinel Golf leads with two Japanese-made options — the Shinto Gauze and the Kontex — that prove the towel category has room for actual craftsmanship. Fyfe Golf turns vintage Guinness bar towels into one-of-a-kind links accessories in a workshop in Scotland. And Vessel's magnetic towel set the standard that half this list is now chasing.

src: Walker Golf Things draw everything by hand, and Blooming Grounds is the fullest expression of that they have put out. Walker are Australian, which is what makes the drop land oddly and also makes it interesting. It went live on 21 August as an ode to spring, to the opening rounds of the season and the flora along the fairways. In Melbourne that is exactly right. Blooming Grounds is a six-piece collection from the Australian brand Walker Golf Things, released on 21 August 2026. Walker describe it as an ode to the golf course itself and to spring. It comprises the Blooming Grounds Knit Polo ($120), the Gardener SS Shirt ($110), the Hedge Hood ($110), the Hedge Featherlite Polo ($100), the Blooming Grounds T-Shirt ($50) and the Hedge Mid Cap ($50).

Walker Golf Things is an Australian company, and August sits at the end of winter in the southern hemisphere, with spring beginning in September. The collection is timed to an Australian spring, which is why a 400gsm brushed-fleece hood appears in a range landing during a northern-hemisphere summer.

For clothing: Left of Field Golf out of Sydney, Walker Golf Things on the Gold Coast, Penta on Sydney's Northern Beaches, Gray + Haast in Burleigh Heads, Okka in Perth, Found Golf in Melbourne, Birds of Condor in Byron Bay, and Midiron, which will not tell you where it is based. For leather and wool goods: Mackem Golf in the Perth hills and Big Dog Golf Co. in Victoria, whose covers are stocked in the pro shops at Royal Melbourne, Barnbougle, Royal Adelaide and Cape Wickham. Most price in Australian dollars, though Left of Field and Birds of Condor both run overseas storefronts that will show you a converted price.

In between, you've got Walker Golf Things , Random Golf Club 's limited Tempo Towel, Birds of Condor , Sunday Golf, Malbon, Ghost Golf's magnetic caddie, Devereux, and Stitch. The spread runs $25 to $50. Small accessory, big personality differentiator.

Jack Fardell competed in the X Games at eleven and has ridden for adidas for years. His father loved golf enough to name his son after the game's greatest player, which Fardell describes with a shrug — "I didn't really have a choice but to play golf." Over the years he found himself in a circle of skaters who all happened to play, and when he landed in Southern California the golf-industry connections started stacking up. Walker Golf Things released its first collection in July 2022.
